title: malus × arnoldiana
intro: Malus × arnoldiana, commonly known as Arnold's crabapple, is a hybrid plant species within the Rosaceae family. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, providing various health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, which contribute to its use in treating conditions like fever, rheumatism, and digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of Malus × arnoldiana include its antimicrobial, antiviral, and antifungal properties, as well as its ability to soothe skin irritations and promote wound healing. The bioactive constituents responsible for these actions include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are present in its leaves, bark, and fruit.
